input.name: image
input.channels: first three image channels; missing channels are zero (Cellpose slices the patch-embedding weights to the given channel count, which equals zero-filling)

output.name: flows
output.consumed_as: cellpose.core.run_net: tiles averaged, then dP = y[:2], cellprob = y[2]

normalize.flat_channel: channels with zero range, or p99 - p1 <= 1e-3, become all zeros
normalize.downsample: percentiles use a strided subsample only when a channel has more than 224**3 pixels

preprocess.resize: cv2.INTER_LINEAR to (int(Ly * rescale), int(Lx * rescale)) when rescale != 1
preprocess.pad: cellpose.transforms.get_pad_yx(div=16, extra=1, min_size=(256, 256)), zero padding, split as evenly as possible
preprocess.tiles: ny = 1 if Ly <= 256 else ceil(1.2 * Ly / 256); starts = linspace(0, Ly - 256, ny).astype(int); same for x
preprocess.blend: cellpose.transforms.average_tiles with _taper_mask(sig=7.5): weight 1 / (1 + exp((|i - 127.5| - 108) / 7.5)) per axis, outer product
preprocess.resample: crop padding, then resize the flows back to the original Ly x Lx with cv2.INTER_LINEAR (resample=True)

postprocess.niter: int(200 / rescale) when resample is True, else 200
postprocess.dynamics: follow_flows on dP * (cellprob > cellprob_threshold) / 5 for niter steps; get_masks_torch; remove_bad_flow_masks(threshold=flow_threshold); fill_holes_and_remove_small_masks(min_size)

desktop.diameter_rule: blank cell_diameter resolves from magnification via spacr.utils._get_diam(magnification, obj='cell')
desktop.normalization_note: the spaCR desktop route normalizes with spacr.io._normalize_img_batch and calls Cellpose with normalize=False; the preprocess block here describes Cellpose's own normalize=True path

output.name: output0
output.layout: rows 0-3 are box cx, cy, w, h in letterboxed input pixels; rows 4.. are per-class scores with sigmoid applied; anchors ordered stride 8, 16, 32
output.head_note: one-to-many head, exactly what desktop predict runs (ultralytics nms=None keeps NMS outside the graph)
output.head: Detect

preprocess.channel_order: RGB into the network. spacr.plaque.detect_wells flips an RGB HxWx3 array to BGR and ultralytics flips it back, so the browser feeds RGB directly
preprocess.grayscale: a single channel is repeated to three

letterbox.ratio: r = min(640 / H, 640 / W) (scale up allowed)
letterbox.resize: cv2.INTER_LINEAR to (round(W * r), round(H * r)); skipped when the size is unchanged
letterbox.padding: rect: dw = (640 - round(W * r)) % 32, dh = (640 - round(H * r)) % 32, so the padded image is only rounded up to a multiple of 32 (ultralytics predict with PyTorch weights, rect=True, auto=True)
letterbox.pad_split: dw /= 2, dh /= 2; top = round(dh - 0.1), bottom = round(dh + 0.1), left = round(dw - 0.1), right = round(dw + 0.1)

postprocess.unletterbox: subtract the left/top padding, divide by r, clip to the image
postprocess.wells: x0, y0, x1, y1 rounded to integers; drop boxes with width or height <= 0; drop boxes with min(w, h) / max(w, h) < min_axis_ratio; sort by (y0, x0)
